intro: INTERGROWTH-21st is the international newborn size and postnatal growth standard developed by the University of Oxford, built from a multi-country, prescriptive-standard cohort in the same tradition as the WHO Child Growth Standards. PediAid links directly to Oxford's own manual-entry tool rather than re-implementing its reference curves, so results always match the official published standard.
indications: Plotting newborn size (weight, length, head circumference) against international standards at birth
Assessing postnatal growth in preterm infants against a standard derived from a healthy, low-risk international population
Cross-checking a growth assessment against a second reference alongside Fenton or WHO charts
Research or audit contexts that specifically call for INTERGROWTH-21st referencing
method: PediAid does not recompute INTERGROWTH-21st centiles itself — tapping through opens Oxford's own manual-entry tool, which takes the infant's measurements and gestational age and returns the official INTERGROWTH-21st percentile.

faqs.q: How is INTERGROWTH-21st different from the Fenton or WHO charts already in PediAid?
faqs.a: All three are growth references built from different cohorts and study designs. PediAid's Fenton and WHO charts are fully interactive in-app; INTERGROWTH-21st is linked directly to Oxford's own tool so the standard stays exactly as published.

faqs.q: Does PediAid calculate INTERGROWTH-21st percentiles itself?
faqs.a: No — it links straight to intergrowth21.ndog.ox.ac.uk's official manual-entry calculator.

faqs.q: When would I use INTERGROWTH-21st instead of Fenton?
faqs.a: Some units and research protocols specifically standardise on INTERGROWTH-21st; PediAid keeps a direct link available so you're not without it, alongside the Fenton and WHO tools built into the app.
